## Description

A clear and concise description of the bug. For example:

I have successfully built the project on Windows 10 using Visual Studio 2019. However, when I run the inference, the generated audio `output.wav` contains static noise and sounds completely different from the reference PyTorch output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Clone the repo (commit hash: a1b2c3d).
2. Build using `cmake --build . --config Release`.
3. Run: `qwen3_tts_ncnn.exe --model ./models/qwen3 --text "Hello world"`
4. Compare `output.wav` with the reference generated by the Python script.

## Expected Behavior

The output audio should be intelligible and match the PyTorch version within a small MSE margin (< 1e-5).

## Actual Behavior

The audio is unintelligible and loud.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **OS** | Windows 10 Pro 64-bit |
| **Compiler** | MSVC 19.28.29914 |
| **ncnn Version** | 20240226 |
| **Build Type** | Release |

## Logs

```
[INFO] Loading model: ./models/qwen3.param
[INFO] Loading weights: ./models/qwen3.bin
[INFO] Model loaded.
[INFO] Generating tokens...
[ERROR] Extractor failed at step 12: -3
[INFO] Audio saved to output.wav
```

## Additional Context

I noticed the extractor returns error code `-3` at step 12 of the generation loop. This error does not occur on the Linux build of the same commit.
